Core shape: `Test.<ID>.ps1` + `.md`; `[MtTest]` PowerShell-class attribute with 16 properties read from the AST; engine-owned service/licence gates; run config = superset of `maester-config.json` passed by discovery or `-Config`; Pester kept as a compatibility provider; result JSON stays 2.x-shaped with additive fields; single-threaded with parallel-readiness rules.

Design now recommends a small C# scheduling core (`Maester.Engine.dll`) inside the module, single-threaded by default in 3.0.

Merill asked (2026-11-05) how undrgrnd-labs/hunch could make the Maester report more insightful, and for a full plan. Published as a private artifact: https://claude.ai/artifact/Xtiz4DyW2n7MEwZujQbNAG (source in that session's scratchpad only; nothing in the repo, per the rule that research stays out of Maester).

Core recommendations: an insights step after the tests (`Insight.<ID>.ps1`, packs can ship them, typed `Insights` records with evidence, prefix `MI.`). Tier A uses only result data: attack scenarios + choke points, most exposed identities, fix-once groups, trends, template summary. Tier B adds bounded reads: measured user impact from sign-in logs and report-only CA results, config snapshot + audit-log change attribution, licence value. Tier C is opt-in question models: critical assets by meaning, suspicious objects, CA intent check, optional AI summary with citation check. Plus a reader profile (infer first, then 5 questions) that re-ranks but never hides findings.

hunch verdict: right pattern, narrow fit (classifying object names and text, multilingual). Not a dependency: created 2026-10-21, PyPI is a 0.0.0 placeholder, needs Python + Rust + 1.4 GB model. Its request shape equals TypeSafe `/v1/systemone`, so one client covers Jev and hunch.

Prerequisites found: only ~70 checks emit affected objects and none record why; `Previous.History` keeps counts only; sign-in/audit logs are read by one check (ASD.ISM-1648); no shared app/SP helper. The affected-objects README still says collection is off by default (stale).

**Added 2026-11-05 (v2 of the artifact):** EntraHound review (take: "unknown is not none" coverage, derived capability edges for a privilege graph, score reasons, exposure as a count, query grammar; skip its A–F grade). Merill's own idea, implementation order from Microsoft Learn prerequisites: recommended tagging the *change* (`Step` attribute + catalogue, same unit as fix-once groups) rather than each test. First pass: 7 chains (compliant devices, risk CA, phishing-resistant MFA, PIM, token protection, email auth, Defender risk) of about 25 changes over about 85 checks. Found 6 prerequisites with no check (device join/enrollment coverage, MFA and phishing-resistant registration, password writeback, Defender–Intune connector). 474 of 623 non-AD guides link Learn (514 URLs) to mine. Decisions now number 11.

**Owner direction (2026-11-05):** Merill: the defender's view (implementation order, prerequisites, readiness) is what others miss and should be Maester's strong point. Artifact v3 reframes the plan around it: Phase 1 leads with the change catalogue + ordered action plan + readiness checks. Working name "Defender's path"; attribute name, product name and catalogue location still open.

**v4 (2026-11-05):** linked to session "Zero trust data in affected objects" (worktree `/Users/merill/github/maester-zta-facts`, branch `feat/zta-affected-object-facts`, uncommitted): `Add-MtAffectedObjectFact` (Name, Value text, Tone Risk/Warning/Good/Info, Source, AsOf) on listed objects; ZTA export adds app/user/device/agent/policy facts. Plan now builds A2 weights, readiness drill-down and Tier C outputs on facts; recommended adding a stable Key + raw value before it ships (not yet sent to that session). Seven chains were hand-picked (3 verified on Learn); 14 more candidate chains listed; systematic sources = Entra/Intune/Purview deployment plans + 514 linked Learn pages. Scoping rules: Not done vs Unknown vs Not checked; `Steps` built from the full inventory; one-check runs get "Before you fix this"; GitHub/AD runs unchanged.

**v5 (2026-11-05):** Merill asked why only Entra docs. Survey of 19 Microsoft 365 source sets: best cross-product ones are the Zero Trust identity and device access series (prerequisite tables), the Zero Trust deployment plan with Microsoft 365, Purview deployment models, Zero Trust for Copilot, archived guest-collaboration pages, Defender XDR pilot, Defender for Office 365 deployment guide, GSA guides, Intune + Defender integration, and the Zero Trust Workshop repo (MIT; `ztw-task-mapping.json` maps ZTA checks to tasks). Most product doc repos are private (`*-pr`); public: entra-docs (MIT), microsoft-365-docs and power-platform (CC BY 4.0). Any Learn page returns Markdown + front matter with `Accept: text/markdown`, so mining and change detection (`updated_at`) work for all products. Catalogue keeps own wording + link, never copied text. Revised estimate 25–30 chains, 70–100 changes, about a third cross-product. Decision 14: a planning-source registry.

**v6 (2026-11-05):** Merill's Learn mirrors are the mining source: `merill/learn-mirror` (MIT tool, sitemaps + TOCs, ETags, one commit per change, 4 runs a day) feeding `intune-docs-mirror` (3,568 pages, 1,699 with a prerequisites section), `defender-docs-mirror` (2,685 / 850) and `entra-docs-mirror`. Proposed new mirrors with draft configs on the artifact: security (Zero Trust, `security-pr`), Purview (`Purview-pr`), Teams admin (`OfficeDocs-SkypeForBusiness-pr`, exclude /platform/), SharePoint + OneDrive (`OfficeDocs-SharePoint-pr`, exclude /dev/), Exchange Online (`OfficeDocs-Exchange-pr`). Change detection via `git log` on cited mirror paths. 23 of the 77 Intune/Defender links in check guides are old redirected URLs. Merill said "Create them". The five scaffolds were tested with an 80-page live crawl each and committed locally in the session scratchpad (`new-mirrors/`). Auto mode blocked `gh repo create --public`. Merill ran the create command himself (2026-11-04 22:43 UTC); security's first crawl got 369 pages, the others were still crawling. Schedules run at :10/:20/:30/:40/:50 past 04, 10, 16 and 22 UTC. Windows Server mirror (for the AD checks, `windowsserverdocs-pr`, about 2,600 pages, 8 TOCs) is scaffolded, tested and committed locally in `new-mirrors/windows-server-docs-mirror`, schedule 05, 11, 17 and 23 UTC; not created yet. The public windowsserverdocs trails Learn. AD guides cite ANSSI (54 links) more than Learn (52 guides with a Learn link). All six new mirrors are live after their first crawls (2026-11-04 UTC): security 369, Purview 1,076, Teams 871, SharePoint 350, Exchange 452, Windows Server 2,589 pages. Purview's first push was blocked by push protection (sample secrets in the `sit-defn-` pages), so its config now excludes `/purview/sit-defn-`. Actions cost: about 46 min per round of nine mirrors, 4 rounds a day, about 5,500–6,000 min/month, free because the repos are public. Proposed but not built: windows-security-docs-mirror (`/windows/security/`, about 370 pages).

**Phase 1 design doc (2026-11-05):** `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md` on branch `docs/defenders-path`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/defenders-path` (from origin/main, uncommitted). 15 decisions in section 17 with recommendations (Step attribute, "Defender's path", lanes = Goals not "paths" because of `-Path`, catalogue in `powershell/assets/steps/`, five statuses incl. Not applicable, Investigate = Unknown, `-Step`/`-IncludePrerequisites`, no new public command). Findings while drafting: NotSelected tests do get NotRun rows but Preview/LongRunning ones get none, so Steps lists tests from the inventory; MT.1021 skips P1+ tenants so the security-defaults conflict needs a new check; MT.1098 partly covers the Defender connector; instance attributes come from the unmerged `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` (Get-MtInstanceAttribute, pack `taxonomy.json`). 3.0 code freeze from 2026-11-07, so this targets 3.1.

**Ruled 2026-11-05: all 15 recommendations accepted; doc status "accepted for implementation".** Fact keys done by the facts session in maester365/maester#2681 (Key + Raw, shared list in formatting-test-results.md "Fact keys"). M1 built in the same worktree, uncommitted: `Step` in C# + schema + reader (lowercased, max 3), `powershell/assets/steps/` (schema, goals.json, entra.json, intune.json: compliant-devices goal, 7 steps), `Get-MtStepCatalog`, `Get-MtStepProblem` (-Coverage only in unit tests, since the build runs on fixture folders), build check, inventory warning, Step in TestShims same-attribute list, 6 tests tagged (MT.1001/1005/1034/1020/1054, CIS.M365.4.1). Learn check changed the design: compliance needs registered + enrolled, not joined, so the readiness step is `intune.devices-compliant`. CIS.M365.4.1 duplicates MT.1054 (same secureByDefault read), so it should become a shim. ZeroTrustAssessmentPack.Tests "skips the family when the module is not installed" fails on Merill's machine because ZTA is installed, and running it starts a real assessment against the connected tenant.

**Measures, not tests (ruled 2026-11-05):** Merill asked why readiness needed new tests; ruling: readiness is a data point. Steps carry `"Measure": { "Key", "MinimumShare" }`; registry `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1` (Key, Function, Title, Unit, Caveat, Service, License, Permission); readers in `internal/services/<service>/` return Count/Total/Objects; no test ID, no pass-rate effect. Later rulings: `devices-compliant` declares `INTUNE_A` (only Intune marks devices compliant; compliance partners need Intune licences too); optional `Caveat` line per measure; MFA measure is `mfa-capable` using `isMfaCapable` (reader `Get-MtMfaCapableShare`), step stays `entra.mfa-registered`. Facts from #2681 attach only to objects the run lists, so readers write facts only after M3 puts measure objects on the Affected objects page (and adds a `user.mfaCapable` key).

**State 2026-11-05:** M2 (43 steps, 8 goals, 43 tests tagged, EIDSCA/ORCA generators read Step), M5 (two readers) and M6 (`build/steps/` tooling + weekly `step-sources.yaml`) were built in parallel sessions and merged into `feat/defenders-path` (draft PR maester365/maester#2683, Auto-fix on). 2026-11-06: M3 (engine: Steps/Goals, schema 2.2, measures run with facts, -Step/-IncludePrerequisites, Get-MtTestPriority), M4 (report: action plan cards/lanes, Before you fix this, overview card) and M7 (docs, generated goal pages) built by worktree agents and merged; all seven milestones on PR 2683, not yet tested against a tenant. Agent worktrees can't run pwsh (guard), so the parent must run Pester. CIS.M365.4.1 shim of MT.1054 is a separate uncommitted change on `claude/elegant-spence-176024`.

**Exception ruled 2026-11-08:** Merill kept MT.1253 (#2694, share of non-compliant devices ≤ 5%) and MT.1266 (#2712, Azure secure score per subscription) as tests, even though the first is the `devices-compliant` measure. Don't ask contributors to turn them into measures.

**Why:** this reopens the 3.0 report proposal's "not taken: AI-written narratives" (decision 1 in the plan).

**How to apply:** the design doc `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md` on `feat/defenders-path` is the source of truth now; follow its decisions (section 17). Related: [[maester-3-report-redesign]], [[maester-marketplace-design]], [[maester-test-taxonomy-research]].

Drafted 2026-10-07 in worktree `.claude/worktrees/maester-3-planning-6643a9`: `docs/proposals/maester-packs-design.md`, on branch `claude/maester-packs-design`, draft PR maester365/maester#2358 stacked on the 3.0 branch (#2334); retarget to main after 3.0 merges. Site mockup canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/9frFAaGEGJgDRXvyst8Ht1 (private).

Owner rulings (2026-10-07): names **pack** / **Maester Packs**; domain **packs.maester.dev** (maester.dev DNS is on Cloudflare); site + small Worker API (+ D1) on Cloudflare, indexing/scanning in GitHub Actions on a public repo (free minutes), keep costs ~$0–5/month; **binaries allowed** but flagged High risk (risk levels Low/Medium/High/Blocked, like skills.sh audits); **v1 runs packs in-process** (isolation via containers later; keep the hosted-service angle generic in public docs); **no verification programme in v1** — badges instead: Official, Microsoft MVP (from the MVP directory API the `merill/newsletter` repo syncs, `app/src/lib/server/authors/mvp-api.ts`), GitHub-verified org. Publisher-side scanners (Codacy/CodeRabbit) shown only as "repository signals".

Design review of 2026-10-07 fully folded in (fork-commit reachability, single loader gate, packs can't pose as built-ins, namespaced connector services `<CODE>.<Platform>`, -IncludePackScopes/MissingScope, phase-1 blocklist with serial/expiry/offline root key, split scan/publish indexer, **no archive mirror (Merill ruled: never cache repos in Cloudflare; a pack gone from GitHub is skipped — NotRun `PackUnavailable` + report warning)**, lifecycle states, numeric IDs, ID ledger, pack API contract, AllSigned/WDAC, terms/takedowns, /p/ routes, maester365 code `MAES`).

**Why:** Merill wants to review the full design before implementation.

Pack test IDs are `MP.<code>.<number>` (e.g. MP.CNT.0001): `MP.` reserved prefix, 2–5 char code (letters/digits, starts with a letter) held by the **publisher (GitHub user/org, numeric owner ID)**, claimed at the first index of any of its repos, first come first served — no PR; one code per owner, permanent, shared by all its packs (index keeps IDs unique across them); every not-listed version gets an indexing status with reason + fix (doc 7.7, packs.maester.dev/status/{owner}/{repo}, Test-MtPack -Remote); `Find-MtPack -Code` / packs.maester.dev/codes/<CODE> lookup; anti-squat: account >30 days, one claim/day, unlisted claims lapse after 90 days. Also ruled: list on first passing install (owner account >30 days), **one new pack per owner per day**, Astro, High-risk packs shown by default, MVP API best-effort, first official pack Google Workspace.

**Under discussion (2026-10-08, community feedback from TestimoX and LeastPrivilegedMSGraph; NOT yet in the design doc — Merill wants the doc updated only after the Discord discussion ends):** outside tools run as their own step and the pack's connector only reads the output file (no signing; schema-version + max-age checks); **hybrid module-backed packs** (code in the publisher's PowerShell module, pack = manifest + build-generated static catalog + docs, `RequiresModules` + `Provider {Module, ApiVersion}`; chosen over Gallery-hosted packs so GitHub/MVP badges still validate); Maester never installs modules (generated `Install-Module` command; missing → tests skipped); publisher Setup tab; rule catalogs; coverage as own result (`NotCollected`, opt-in CI); own auth libs wrapped as connectors + run-scoped cache; permissions beyond Graph (Entra/Azure RBAC/Exchange roles, `MissingPermission`); connection targets via `Connections.<Service>`/parameter kinds/families. Mode names proposed: code = **Script pack** / **Module pack**; data = **Live** / **Import** / **Collect** (optional Collect hook once per run + Release hook, off by default). Summarised (with two SVG diagrams) in the overview HTML's "Under discussion" section.

**How to apply:** Only owner-side setup is still open (GitHub App, signing key, Cloudflare). Never raise or record the existing `InvokeMaester` PostHog run telemetry in the Packs design — Merill ruled it out of scope (opt-out is already documented). Don't implement until he rules. Keep maester-cloud internals out of public docs, as with [[maester-3-design]].

Redesign of how Maester tests are grouped and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and frameworks. Started as research on 2026-10-11; the same day Merill told me to implement it.

**Research (private):** maester-cloud branch `claude/test-taxonomy-research` (commit 348d21c6, local only, not pushed), worktree `/Users/merill/github/maester-cloud/.claude/worktrees/test-taxonomy-research`, folder `docs/test-taxonomy-research/` (`clean-slate-attribute-design.html` is the design review; vendor survey; `notes/`). Private artifacts: design https://claude.ai/artifact/UyXNL9LJsatxpuoWrxUuAY, survey https://claude.ai/artifact/B96aZbWKpSJ1omXmp3qJkD, test explorer (all 746 tests, filter/pivot by attribute, ATT&CK, benchmark) https://claude.ai/artifact/BqFSiPXCb8pLJ8M3DAHvQz — also `maester-test-explorer.html` in the research folder (commit 91c35b84); rebuild with scratch script `build_explorer_data.py` from `module/Maester.TestCatalog.json` plus the rater values.

**Implementation (Maester):** branch `claude/maester-3-test-attributes`, stacked on the 3.0 branch (`claude/maester-3-planning-6643a9`, PR 2334), worktree `/Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/maester-3-test-attributes`. Local commits only; not pushed, no PR. Contract files: `docs/proposals/maester-3.0-test-attributes.md` (design), `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (rubric), `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1` (products/features/areas/resource types), `powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json` (ATT&CK 19.2 trimmed).

**Owner rulings (2026-10-11):**
- OK to change the existing `Category` and `Tag`.
- Research must NOT go into the Maester repo; maester-cloud is fine. Only the final redesign goes into Maester.
- A test can span products (e.g. Entra ID and Intune): handled with single `Product` + optional `RelatedProduct` list.
- Fill in values for all tests; define a rubric per attribute; add unit tests that fail when a test does not meet the rubric.
- Add a review step where an AI reviewer checks new or changed test attributes against the rubric and fails otherwise; he will supply an API key (I defaulted to the Claude API, secret `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, model `claude-opus-5-5`; the repo's only earlier AI script used Gemini as a one-off).
- Maester Cloud (closed source, `jozrahq/maester-cloud`) is his hosted product, positioned against Tenable/Wiz; keep it out of public Maester docs.

**Design as implemented in the spec:** remove `Category` (result `Block` derived from Product) and `Preview` (→ `Lifecycle`); `Tag` = owner's free labels, built-ins carry none; 2.x tags keep selecting through `Maester.LegacyTags.json`; `Product` is a registry key; new `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, `Permission`, `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy`; typed selectors `-Product/-Feature/-Area/-Severity/-Suite`; `suite.json` `Frameworks` + framework files for CIS/CISA.

**Things I learned that are easy to lose:**
- The Zero Trust Assessment public repo has no written rubric (only ValidateSet values); I calibrated on its 336 tests (risk High 60/Med 35/Low 6; user impact Low 66/Med 27/High 7; cost Low 54/Med 37/High 9). Merill believes a ZTA rubric exists; ask him for it if alignment matters.

# Design: the Zero Trust Assessment pack

> **Status: DRAFT.** Drafted 2026-10-19 against the Maester Packs design
> ([maester-packs-design.md](maester-packs-design.md), draft PR #2358) and the Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment
> at commit `fa6ffc8` of [microsoft/zerotrustassessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)
> (module version 2.6.0). The owner ruled on 2026-10-19 that the pack ships with Maester and is opt-in.

## 1. Summary

Maester ships an official pack, `maester.zero-trust-assessment`, that runs Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment
(ZTA) and shows each of its results as a Maester result row, `ZTA.<ZTA test ID>`. It lives in
`packs/zero-trust-assessment/`. It does not copy ZTA's code: it runs the `ZeroTrustAssessment` module the user
installs, or reads a report ZTA already wrote.

- **One family test.** The pack is a single 3.0 native test, `ZTA`, whose instance source gets ZTA's
  report and returns one instance per result. Families already exist in 3.0, so the pack runs on today's engine
  as a custom test (`Invoke-MtTest -Path packs/zero-trust-assessment/tests`) and needs nothing from the pack
  loader beyond loading its one file.
- **Opt-in through `LongRunning`.** The family is `LongRunning`, so `Invoke-Maester` leaves it out unless the
  run names `ZTA`, sets `-IncludeLongRunning`, or turns either on in config. Its timeout is
  `Execution.LongRunningTimeoutSeconds`.
- **Import or collect.** With `GlobalSettings."ZeroTrustAssessment.ReportPath"` set, the pack reads that report
  (the recommendation for CI). Without it, the pack runs ZTA in a child `pwsh` process and reads the report it
  writes.
- **A static catalog.** `catalog.json`, generated from the module by `build/zta/Update-MtZtaCatalog.ps1`, lists
  the 336 tests with title, pillar, risk level, impact, cost, service and licence, for the pack's listing.

## 2. What the Zero Trust Assessment is

ZTA is Microsoft's PowerShell module (MIT licence) that rates a Microsoft 365 tenant against its Zero Trust
guidance. 3.0 borrowed its test model, so the two are close:

| | ZTA | Maester 3.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A test | `Test-Assessment.<id>.ps1` with `[ZtTest(...)]` + `.md` | `Test.<ID>.ps1` with `[MaesterTest(...)]` + `.md` |
| Rating | `RiskLevel`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Pillar`, `Category`, `SfiPillar` | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` |
| Gates | `Service` (all-of), `CompatibleLicense`, `TenantType` | `Service`, `License`, `TenantType` |
| Result helper | `Add-ZtTestResultDetail` | `Add-MtTestResultDetail` |
| Statuses | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, Planned | Passed, Failed, Investigate, Skipped, Error, NotRun |

The difference that decides the integration is how ZTA gets its data. `Invoke-ZtAssessment` runs in stages:
export the tenant's data (Graph, Azure, Exchange, Security & Compliance, SharePoint, AIP) into JSON files, load
them into a DuckDB database, run every test against the database with `-Database`, then write
`zt-export/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.json` and an HTML report. The tests cannot run without the export and the
database, and the module carries native DuckDB binaries, PSFramework, and exact pins on the Graph, Exchange
Online and Az modules, which it downloads into its own cache and loads in a fixed MSAL order.

## 3. Options considered

| Option | What it means | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Port the tests to Maester | Rewrite 336 tests against `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` | No: they query ZTA's database, and two copies would drift |
| One Maester test per ZTA test, calling ZTA in-process | Generated `Test.ZTA.<id>.ps1` files that call ZTA's private test functions | No: needs ZTA's private functions and database, and ZTA's pinned modules cannot share a process with Maester's |
| **Run ZTA, map its report** | Run `Invoke-ZtAssessment` (or read its output) and turn each report row into a Maester row | **Chosen**: uses only ZTA's public commands and its report, which is versioned data |

Within the chosen option, the report is mapped by a family test rather than 336 generated test files. A
family runs its instance source once under its own timeout, which is exactly the "collect once, then report
many" shape ZTA needs, and it works on the 3.0 engine today. The Collect hook in the packs overview's
"Under discussion" section would give the same shape to generated per-test files; if it lands, the pack can
move to it without changing the result IDs.

Each folder here is a [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/packs) that is part of the Maester module:

## Parameters

A test's `param()` block lists the values a user can tune per tenant: thresholds, switches, objects to exclude.
Values come from the run configuration or from `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`; a test always has to run with none
set, using its defaults.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups,

    # How strictly to evaluate.
    [ValidateSet('Strict', 'Lenient')]
    [string] $Mode = 'Strict'
)
```

Rules:

- Types are `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string` or `string[]`.
- Defaults are constants. No parameter is mandatory.
- Every parameter has a description: a `#` comment on the line directly above it, or `.PARAMETER` help. Only
  the comment line nearest the parameter is read, so keep the comment to one line or use `.PARAMETER`.
  `Get-MtTest` shows the description.
- Give thresholds a `ValidateRange`. A `ValidateSet` makes the parameter a list of choices.
- `Instance` and every name that starts with `Mt` belong to the engine and cannot be set.

Set values in the config:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "CONTOSO.1002", "Parameters": { "ReasonMarker": "Off:" } },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
  ]
}
```

The engine checks each value against the `param()` block before the test runs. A name the test does not have,
a fraction for an `int`, a number for a `string`, a string for a `bool` or `switch`, or a value outside the
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet` gives that test an `Error` row with reason `InvalidConfiguration`; the run
carries on. A `string[]` parameter accepts one string or a list. The effective values, and where each came from
(`Default`, `Config` or `Parameter`), are written to the result row's `Parameters`.

### Parameter kinds

`[MaesterParameter(Kind = '...')]` says what a string parameter holds, so a user interface can offer a picker
and the engine can check the value's shape:

| Kind | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Entra.User` | User object ID |
| `Entra.Group` | Group object ID |
| `Entra.ServicePrincipal` | Service principal object ID |
| `Entra.Application` | Application object ID |
| `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy` | Conditional Access policy ID |
| `Entra.NamedLocation` | Named location ID |
| `Entra.Domain` | Domain name |
| `Entra.DirectoryRole` | Directory role definition ID |
| `Azure.Subscription` | Subscription ID |
| `Azure.ResourceGroup` | Resource group ID (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`) |
| `Azure.Resource` | Azure resource ID |

A value that does not match the kind's pattern (for example a malformed GUID) is `InvalidConfiguration`. In the
config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

## Families: one test, several results

Some checks produce one result per item: per drift folder, per recommendation, per user. Declare
`InstanceSource` with the name of a function in the same file. The engine calls that function when the test
runs (never during discovery) and runs the test once per object it returns, passing the object as `$Instance`.

```powershell
function Get-ContosoAdminUnit {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    foreach ($unit in Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'directory/administrativeUnits') {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id    = $unit.id                     # required: the instance suffix
            Title = "Administrative unit '$($unit.displayName)' is restricted"   # optional
            Data  = $unit                        # optional: anything the test needs
        }
    }
}

function Test-ContosoAdminUnitRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CONTOSO.2001',
        Title = 'Administrative units are restricted.',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        Service = 'Graph',
        InstanceSource = 'Get-ContosoAdminUnit'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The administrative unit to check, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance
    )

    $restricted = [bool]$Instance.Data.isMemberManagementRestricted
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Member management restricted: $restricted"
    return $restricted
}
```

The instance object has:

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | Yes | The suffix. The row's ID is `<parent ID>.<Id>`, for example `CONTOSO.2001.4f6c...`. It must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$` and be unique within the family. |
| `Title` | No | The instance's title. Defaults to `-TestTitle` from the helper, then the attribute's title. |
| `Severity` | No | The instance's severity, used when the config sets none. |
| `Tag` | No | Extra tags written to the instance's row. |
| `Fields` | No | Facts about the instance that a report can group or filter by, as a hashtable of names to strings or arrays of strings, for example `@{ Pillar = 'Identity'; Category = 'Access control' }`. Written to the row's `Fields`; other values are left out. |
| `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `RelatedProduct`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` | No | What this instance is about, when that differs from its family, with the same keys as the attribute. A family that reads results from another tool, such as the Zero Trust Assessment pack, places each result under its own product this way. A value the taxonomy does not know is left out, and the row keeps the family's. |
| `Control` | No | The requirements this instance implements, as one `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>` value or a list, for example `'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`. They replace the family's `Control`, and the row gets its own `Benchmark` and the requirements' `Related` references, as a test does (see [What the result gets](#what-the-result-gets)). A family that reads another tool's results per policy, such as the ScubaGear pack, maps each result to its requirement this way. A value that is not written `<framework-key>:<id>`, or that names a requirement the framework file does not have, is left out; when none is left, the row keeps the family's `Control` and `Benchmark`. |
| `Data` | No | Anything the test needs. It is not written to the result. |

Each instance row carries `ParentId` (the family's ID) and `InstanceId`. When the family does not produce
instance rows, the result has one row on the parent ID instead:

| What happened | Row on the parent ID |
| --- | --- |
| The family was not selected, was disabled, or a gate failed | The usual `NotRun` or `Skipped` reason |
| The instance source returned nothing | `Skipped` with `NoInstances` |
| The instance source threw, did not finish within the family's timeout, or ended with `exit` | `Error` with `InstanceSourceFailed` |
| An instance `Id` is missing, invalid or repeated | `Error` with `InvalidInstanceId` |

The instance source runs under the same timeout as the test (the family's `TimeoutSeconds`, or the run's
`Execution` timeout). The source gets that long to return, and then each instance gets that long to run.

Selection and configuration understand families:

- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001` or `-TestId 'CONTOSO.2001.*'` selects the whole family.
- `-TestId CONTOSO.2001.abc` runs only that instance; the others get `NotRun` rows with reason `NotSelected`.
- `-ExcludeTestId` and `"Enabled": false` on an instance ID drop that instance after the source has run.
- A `TestSettings` row on an instance ID wins over a row on the parent ID. Its `Parameters` and
  `TimeoutSeconds` apply to that instance only; a parameter it does not name keeps the value of the family's row.
- IDs under a family's parent are never reported as unknown, even if that instance does not exist in this run.

## Settings shared by many tests

Read tenant-wide settings from `GlobalSettings` in the config with `Get-MtSetting`:

```powershell
$accounts = Get-MtSetting -Name EmergencyAccessAccounts
$siteUrl  = Get-MtSetting -Name 'Contoso.SiteUrl' -Default 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com'
```

When the config does not set the value, `Get-MtSetting` returns Maester's default for the settings it knows,
else `-Default`. Use a `Namespace.Key` name for your own settings. Prefer a test parameter when the value
belongs to one test.

## What a custom test can call

Each custom test file is loaded into its own private module. It can call every command Maester exports,
including `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, `Get-MtSetting`, `Get-MtTenantContext`,
`Test-MtConnection`, `Get-MtLicenseInformation`, `Get-MtUser`, `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy` and
`Invoke-MtTest`. It cannot call Maester's private functions, and it cannot replace a Maester command.

Functions defined in the same file are visible to the test. Functions in another test file are not. To share
code between files, put it in a helper `.ps1` (one that is not named `Test.*.ps1`) and dot-source it from
inside the test function: `. "$PSScriptRoot/Contoso.Helpers.ps1"`. `$PSScriptRoot` is the test file's folder.

To reuse a built-in check, run it through the engine instead of calling its function:

```powershell
$row = Invoke-MtTest -Id MT.1005
$row.Result   # Passed, Failed, Skipped, ...
```

The built-in check functions are no longer exported in 3.0, and they no longer contain their own connection
checks, so calling one directly is not supported.

## A suite manifest for your folder

# Microsoft Graph Agent Skill

Search, look up, and call any of the 27,700+ Microsoft Graph APIs — all locally, no network calls needed. Use the three search commands to find the right endpoint, check permissions and parameters, then optionally execute calls directly or hand off to a Graph MCP server.

## What's Included

The Microsoft Graph API has **27,700+ endpoints** updated weekly — well past LLM training cutoffs. This skill bundles the complete API surface as local indexes that you search instantly with no network calls.

| Index | Count | What it contains |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI endpoints | 27,700+ | Path, method, summary, description, permission scopes |
| Endpoint docs | 6,200+ | Permissions (delegated/app), query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties |
| Resource schemas | 4,200+ | All properties with types, supported `$filter` operators, default/select-only flags |
| Community samples | Growing | Hand-verified queries mapping natural-language tasks to exact API calls |

## How to Run

The `msgraph` CLI is bundled with this skill. Run all commands through the launcher script in this skill's directory:

- **macOS / Linux**: `bash <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.sh <command> [args...]`
- **Windows**: `powershell <path-to-this-skill>/scripts/run.ps1 <command> [args...]`

For example, to search for mail-related APIs on macOS:

```
bash /home/user/.opencode/skills/msgraph/scripts/run.sh openapi-search --query "send mail"
```

In all examples below, `msgraph` is shorthand for the full launcher invocation.

## Finding the Right API

This is the primary purpose of the skill. Follow this progressive lookup strategy — each level adds detail:

1. **Your own knowledge** — try first for well-known endpoints (`/me`, `/users`, `/groups`).
2. **`sample-search`** — curated, hand-verified samples. Highest quality. Use for common tasks and multi-step workflows.
3. **`api-docs-search`** — per-endpoint permissions, supported query parameters, required headers, default vs `$select`-only properties, and resource property details with filter operators.
4. **`openapi-search`** — full catalog of 27,700 Graph APIs. Use when you cannot find the endpoint any other way.
5. **Reference files** — concept docs on query parameters, advanced queries, paging, batching, throttling, errors, and best practices. Read only when you need specific guidance.

This order is guidance — adapt based on the task. For example, jump straight to `api-docs-search` if you already know the endpoint but need its permissions.

### sample-search

Search curated community samples that map natural-language tasks to exact Microsoft Graph API queries:

```
msgraph sample-search --query "conditional access policies"
msgraph sample-search --product entra
msgraph sample-search --query "managed devices" --product intune
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--query` | Free-text search (searches intent and query fields) |
| `--product` | Filter by product: `entra`, `intune`, `exchange`, `teams`, `sharepoint`, `security`, `general` |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |

At least one of `--query` or `--product` is required. Results include multi-step workflows.

### api-docs-search

Look up detailed documentation for a specific endpoint or resource type:

```
msgraph api-docs-search --endpoint /users --method GET
msgraph api-docs-search --resource user
msgraph api-docs-search --query "ConsistencyLevel"
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint` | Search by endpoint path (e.g. `/users`, `/me/messages`) |
| `--resource` | Search by resource type name (e.g. `user`, `group`, `message`) |
| `--method` | Filter by HTTP method: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` |
| `--query` | Free-text search across all fields |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 10) |

At least one of `--endpoint`, `--resource`, or `--query` is required.

**Endpoint results** include: required permissions (delegated work/school, delegated personal, application), supported OData query parameters, required headers, default properties, and endpoint-specific notes.

**Resource results** include: all properties with types, supported `$filter` operators (eq, ne, startsWith, etc.), and whether each property is returned by default or requires `$select`.

### openapi-search

Search the full OpenAPI catalog of 27,700 Microsoft Graph APIs:

```
msgraph openapi-search --query "send mail"
msgraph openapi-search --resource messages --method GET
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--query` | Free-text search (searches path, summary, description) |
| `--resource` | Filter by resource name (e.g. `users`, `groups`, `messages`) |
| `--method` | Filter by HTTP method |
| `--limit` | Max results (default 20) |

At least one of `--query`, `--resource`, or `--method` is required.

## Using with MCP Servers

If the agent has access to a Microsoft Graph MCP server (such as [lokka.dev](https://lokka.dev) or any other Microsoft Graph MCP server), use the search tools above to find the right endpoint, permissions, and request syntax, then use the information with the MCP server for execution.

In this mode, **no authentication through this skill is needed**. The skill acts purely as a knowledge layer — the MCP server handles authentication and API execution.

## Direct Microsoft Graph API Execution

When no Graph MCP server is available, this skill can authenticate to Microsoft 365 and execute Microsoft Graph API calls directly.

### Authentication

The tool supports **delegated (user)** and **app-only (application)** authentication, auto-detected from environment variables.

**Quick start:**

```
msgraph auth status          # check if signed in
msgraph auth signin          # sign in (opens browser) - recommended
msgraph auth signin --device-code  # sign in via device code (headless)
msgraph auth signout         # clear the session
```

- **Delegated auth** (default): Interactive browser sign-in, with device code fallback for headless environments. Supports incremental consent — on 403, the tool re-authenticates with required scopes and retries automatically.
- **App-only auth**: Auto-detected when `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`, `MSGRAPH_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`, or `MSGRAPH_AUTH_METHOD=managed-identity` is set. Requires `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID`.

For detailed authentication configuration including certificates, managed identity, workload identity federation, and all environment variables, see [references/docs/authentication.md](references/docs/authentication.md).

### Making Graph API Calls

**IMPORTANT**: Run `msgraph auth status` before the first `graph-call` in a session to verify authentication.

```
msgraph graph-call <METHOD> <URL> [flags]
```

#### Read Operations

```
msgraph graph-call GET /me
msgraph graph-call GET /users --select "displayName,mail" --top 10
msgraph graph-call GET /me/messages --filter "isRead eq false" --top 5 --select "subject,from,receivedDateTime"
msgraph graph-call GET /users --filter "startsWith(displayName,'John')"
```

#### Write Operations

**IMPORTANT**: YOU MUST ask the user for confirmation before any write operation. Write operations require the `--allow-writes` flag.

```
msgraph graph-call POST /me/sendMail --body '{"message":{"subject":"Hello","body":{"content":"Hi"},"toRecipients":[{"emailAddress":{"address":"user@example.com"}}]}}' --allow-writes
msgraph graph-call PATCH /me --body '{"jobTitle":"Engineer"}' --allow-writes
```

**DELETE is always blocked** regardless of flags.

#### graph-call Flags

| Flag | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `--select` | OData $select | `--select "displayName,mail"` |
| `--filter` | OData $filter | `--filter "isRead eq false"` |
| `--top` | OData $top (limit results) | `--top 10` |
| `--expand` | OData $expand | `--expand "members"` |
| `--orderby` | OData $orderby | `--orderby "displayName desc"` |
| `--api-version` | `v1.0` or `beta` (default: beta) | `--api-version v1.0` |
| `--scopes` | Request additional permission scopes | `--scopes "Mail.Read"` |
| `--headers` | Custom HTTP headers | `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"` |
| `--body` | Request body (JSON) | `--body '{"key":"value"}'` |
| `--output` | `json` (default) or `raw` | `--output raw` |
| `--allow-writes` | Allow POST/PUT/PATCH (requires user confirmation) | |

## Critical Rules

### Always (search and knowledge)

1. **Never guess or fabricate Microsoft Graph endpoints** — always verify via search before calling. This skill exists because agents hallucinate endpoints; use it.
2. **Use the progressive lookup strategy** — start with what you know, then sample-search, api-docs-search, openapi-search as needed.
3. **Use `--select`** to reduce response size — only request fields you need.
4. **Use `--top`** to limit results — avoid fetching thousands of records.
5. **ConsistencyLevel header** is required for `$count` and `$search` on directory objects (users, groups, etc.). Use `--headers "ConsistencyLevel:eventual"`.
6. **Default API version is beta** — use `--api-version v1.0` for production-stable endpoints.

### When using direct execution (graph-call)

7. **Check auth status** before the first `graph-call` in a session.
8. **GET is the default** — no special flags needed.
9. **Write operations require `--allow-writes`** — YOU MUST confirm with the user first.
10. **DELETE is always blocked** — inform the user this is not supported.
11. **403 triggers automatic re-auth** — the tool requests additional scopes and retries (delegated auth only).
12. **All output is JSON** — parse `statusCode` and `body` fields from the response.

## Error Handling

| Status | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Token expired | Run `msgraph auth signin` again |
| 403 | Insufficient permissions | Tool auto-retries with incremental consent. If still fails, user needs admin consent. |
| 404 | Resource not found | Verify the endpoint path |
| 429 | Rate limited | Wait for Retry-After duration, then retry |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID` | Custom Entra ID app client ID | Microsoft Graph CLI Tools app |
| `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID` | Target tenant ID (required for app-only) | `common` |
| `MSGRAPH_API_VERSION` | Default API version | `beta` |
| `MSGRAPH_INDEX_DB_PATH` | Path to OpenAPI index database | Auto-detected |
| `MSGRAPH_SAMPLES_DB_PATH` | Path to samples index database | Auto-detected |
| `MSGRAPH_API_DOCS_DB_PATH` | Path to API docs index database | Auto-detected |
| `MSGRAPH_NO_TOKEN_CACHE` | Disable persistent token cache (in-memory only) | `false` |

For the full list of authentication environment variables, see [references/docs/authentication.md](references/docs/authentication.md).

## Compatibility

Search tools run fully offline with no network access required. Direct API execution requires network access to `login.microsoftonline.com` and `graph.microsoft.com`. A system browser is used for interactive auth; falls back to device code flow in headless environments.

# Design: tenant pins (tests Maester writes for your tenant)

> **Status: DRAFT.** Drafted 2026-11-09 against Maester 3.0 on `main`. Nothing is implemented. Section 17 lists
> the decisions the owner needs to make; each has a recommendation.

## 1. Summary

Maester's checks today ask one question of every tenant: *is this setting configured well?* They are the same
for everyone. This design adds a second question that only the tenant can answer: *is this still the way we
set it up?* Maester scans the tenant once, works out which objects its security depends on, writes down how
each one looks today, and from then on fails a test when one of them changes.

- **A pin** is one recorded fact about one object: "contoso.com is federated with issuer
  `http://sts.contoso.com/adfs/services/trust` and signing certificate `3F2A…91`", or "the group
  *CA-Exclude-BreakGlass* has exactly these two members". Each pin carries the reason Maester picked it.
- **Maester picks what to pin by following dependencies.** It starts from the controls that protect the tenant
  (Conditional Access, MFA, PIM, Intune compliance, Defender policy) and from the ways in (federation, trusted
  certificate authorities, partner tenants, privileged apps), and pins every object those depend on. A group is
  pinned because it is excluded from the MFA policy, not because of its name.
- **Pins are data, not code.** `New-MtTenantPin` writes a pin file, `maester-pins.<tenantId>.json`, next to
  `maester-config.json`. Maester ships one family test per *pin kind* (federated domain, CA exclusion group,
  Intune script, …); each family reads the pin file and produces one row per pin, such as
  `MT.13xx.contoso.com`. No generated code runs, and every improvement to a pin kind reaches every tenant.
- **A change fails the row and says what moved.** The row shows the pinned value, the current value and why it
  matters, and (milestone 3) who changed it, read from the audit logs. A change that weakens security is
  `Failed`; a change that tightens it is `Investigate`.
- **Accepting a change is a commit.** `Update-MtTenantPin` re-records the pins the admin accepts and adds
  objects that have become critical since the last scan. In a repository the update is a pull request, so the
  review of the change and the approval of the new state are the same step.
- **An agent skill adds judgement on top.** A user-facing skill lets the admin's AI agent propose pins that
  dependencies cannot find (the payroll app's credentials, the CFO's authentication methods) using the same
  pin kinds, and write a custom test with `New-MtTest` when no kind fits. The AI proposes; the pin file is the
  contract; nothing at run time depends on a model.

## 2. The problem

Generic checks cannot see what a tenant relies on. Three examples:

- **Federation.** Maester can say that a tenant should not federate with an insecure IdP. It cannot say that
  contoso.com's token-signing certificate is `3F2A…91` and nothing else. Replacing that certificate, or
  federating a second domain with an IdP someone else runs, lets that party sign tokens for the tenant's users
  (MITRE T1484.002, T1606.002). Every setting stays "valid", so every generic check still passes.
- **Exclusions.** MT.1005 checks that every CA policy excludes a break-glass account. Nothing notices when a
  third user joins the exclusion group. The membership of an exclusion group *is* the policy, and adding a
  member is the quietest way around MFA.
- **Indirect dependencies.** A CA policy that requires a compliant device is only as strong as the compliance
  policies that define "compliant" and the groups they are assigned to. Removing the BitLocker requirement from
  a compliance policy, or editing the assignment filter, weakens the CA policy without touching it.

Admins could write these tests themselves: MT.1060 already compares a `baseline.json` with a `current.json`.
Few do, because they would have to know which objects matter, export them, and keep the files current. This
design moves all three jobs into Maester.

What this is not:

- Not a replacement for the generic checks: a pinned value can be bad. Pins say "unchanged", not "good".
- Not real time. Pins are checked when Maester runs (typically daily). A SIEM alert on "Set federation
  settings on domain" is faster; a pin catches changes made by any route, needs no SIEM, and states the
  approved value.
- Not a backup or desired-state tool. Pins never write to the tenant and record only what matters to security.
  Microsoft365DSC and Microsoft's tenant configuration management APIs (section 15) cover whole-tenant snapshots.

## 3. Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Anchor | An object security depends on: a federated domain, an exclusion group, a trusted CA, an Intune script. |
| Pin | One anchor plus the properties recorded for it, the reason it was picked and who approved it. |
| Pin kind | A kind of anchor that Maester knows how to find, record and compare, such as `entra.domain-federation`. Each kind is one family test. |
| Pin file | `maester-pins.<tenantId>.json`: every pin for one tenant. Owned by the admin, kept in their Maester folder. |
| Scan | `New-MtTenantPin` or `Update-MtTenantPin -Discover`: finding anchors and recording them. |
| Accept | Recording the current value of a changed pin, so that it passes again. |

## 4. Options considered

| Option | What it means | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An AI agent writes a test per anchor | A skill reads the tenant and writes `Test.CONTOSO.<n>.ps1` files with the values in the code | No as the main route: a different result on every run, hundreds of files to review, and nothing improves when Maester does. Kept as a proposal layer (section 12). |
| Generate static test files from templates | `New-MtTenantPin` writes one test file per anchor | No: the same staleness. A fix to how federation is compared would mean regenerating every tenant's files, and admins would edit them and lose updates. |
| **Pin file + one family per pin kind** | The scan writes data; Maester's families read it | **Chosen.** The file is small and reviewable in a diff, the logic is versioned and unit tested in Maester, and families already exist in 3.0. |
| Build on Microsoft's configuration monitors | Create UTCM monitors (`/admin/configurationManagement`) and read their drifts | Not now: beta, needs write permission to create monitors (Maester is read-only), and it watches whatever resources it is told to, without knowing why one matters. Revisit as a reader (section 15). |

## 5. End to end

```powershell
Connect-Maester
New-MtTenantPin                      # scan, then write ./maester-pins.<tenantId>.json
Invoke-Maester                       # every pin passes: nothing has changed yet
```

`New-MtTenantPin` prints what it found, grouped by kind, with the reason for each:

```text
Pinned 63 objects in contoso.onmicrosoft.com (9f1c…)

  Federated domains                 2   contoso.com, fabrikam.com (AD FS)
  Domain federation settings        2   issuer, signing and next signing certificate
  Conditional Access policies      14   12 enabled, 2 report-only
  CA exclusion groups               4   CA-Exclude-BreakGlass excluded from 14 policies
  CA trusted locations              2   HQ-Egress used to skip MFA in 'CA003 Require MFA'
  Emergency access accounts         2   from EmergencyAccessAccounts
  Privileged role members          11   Global Administrator (3), Privileged Role Administrator (2), …
  Privileged apps                   6   hold RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory or similar
  Intune compliance policies        5   CA003 requires a compliant device
  Intune scripts                    3   'Set-Baseline.ps1' runs as SYSTEM on All devices
  …

Review the file, commit it, and run Invoke-Maester. Accept a change later with Update-MtTenantPin.
```

From then on:

1. **A run** reads the pin file for the connected tenant and checks each pin. Unchanged pins pass.
2. **A change** fails that pin's row (or makes it `Investigate`, section 7.3). The row shows a table of
   pinned and current values, why the object matters, and how to accept the change.
3. **The admin accepts it**: `Update-MtTenantPin -Id MT.13xx.contoso.com` records the current value, with
   `PinnedAt` and `PinnedBy`. `Update-MtTenantPin -Discover` also adds anchors that are new since the last scan
   (a new CA policy, a new exclusion group) and retires pins whose object is gone, after the admin confirms.
4. **In CI** the pin file lives in the same repository as the config. Accepting is a commit, so a pull request
   is the review. A maester-action option that opens that pull request with the proposed update is a follow-up
   in that repository.

## 6. The pin file

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pins-1.0.json",
  "SchemaVersion": "1.0",
  "TenantId": "9f1c0000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
  "CreatedAt": "2026-11-09T04:12:00Z",
  "CreatedBy": "Maester 3.1.0",
  "Pins": [
    {
      "Kind": "entra.domain-federation",
      "Target": { "Id": "contoso.com", "DisplayName": "contoso.com" },
      "Source": "Discovered",
      "Severity": "High",
      "Reason": "contoso.com is federated with AD FS. A different issuer or signing certificate lets whoever holds it sign in as any user in the domain.",
      "PinnedAt": "2026-11-09T04:12:00Z",
      "PinnedBy": "admin@contoso.com",
      "Expected": {
        "issuerUri": "http://sts.contoso.com/adfs/services/trust",
        "passiveSignInUri": "https://sts.contoso.com/adfs/ls/",
        "signingCertificate": { "Thumbprint": "3F2A…91", "NotAfter": "2027-04-02" },
        "nextSigningCertificate": null,
        "federatedIdpMfaBehavior": "rejectMfaByFederatedIdp",
        "preferredAuthenticationProtocol": "wsFed",
        "promptLoginBehavior": "nativeSupport"
      }
    },
    {
      "Kind": "entra.ca-exclusion-group",
      "Target": { "Id": "4b9e…", "DisplayName": "CA-Exclude-BreakGlass" },
      "Source": "Discovered",
      "Severity": "High",
      "Reason": "Excluded from 14 enabled Conditional Access policies, including 'CA001 Require MFA for admins'. A new member skips all of them.",
      "PinnedAt": "2026-11-09T04:12:00Z",
      "PinnedBy": "admin@contoso.com",
      "Expected": {
        "groupTypes": [],
        "isAssignableToRole": true,
        "membershipRule": null,
        "members": [ { "Id": "a1…", "DisplayName": "bg-01@contoso.onmicrosoft.com" },
                     { "Id": "b2…", "DisplayName": "bg-02@contoso.onmicrosoft.com" } ],
        "owners": []
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- **One tenant per file, always named by tenant ID.** Maester looks for `maester-pins.<tenantId>.json` the way
  it looks for `maester-config.<tenantId>.json`: in the test folder and upwards. There is no unnamed default, so
  one tenant's pins can never be read for another. `Invoke-Maester -PinPath` points elsewhere. A file whose
  `TenantId` does not match the connection gives every pin family an `Error` row with reason
  `InvalidConfiguration`.
- **`Target.Id` is stable**: an object ID, or a domain name for domains. Renames do not break pins;
  `DisplayName` is only a label and is refreshed on update. The row ID is `<family ID>.<Target.Id>` with the
  instance grammar applied (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`).
- **`Expected` holds normalised values** (section 7.2): sorted lists, certificates as thumbprint and expiry,
  script bodies as a SHA-256 hash, no timestamps.
- **`Source`** is `Discovered` (the scan), `Agent` (proposed by the skill and accepted) or `User` (added with
  `Add-MtTenantPin`). The scan never removes `Agent` or `User` pins on its own.
- **`Enabled: false`** keeps a pin in the file without checking it. Excluding a row with the usual
  `TestSettings` or `-ExcludeTestId` also works.
- **It is sensitive.** The file is a map of the tenant's soft spots: exclusion groups, break-glass IDs,
  trusted IP ranges. It holds no secrets, but it belongs in the same private repository as the config. Anyone
  who can change it can accept a change, so the docs say to protect the branch.

## 7. Pin kinds

A pin kind is the unit Maester ships. Each one has:

| Part | Job |
| --- | --- |
| Discover | Given the tenant, return the anchors of this kind, each with a severity and a reason (section 8). |
| Capture | Read one anchor's current state and normalise it. The same function feeds the scan and every run. |
| Compare | Compare `Expected` with the captured state and return the changes, each with a direction. |
| Guide | The family's `Test.<ID>.md`: what this kind is, why it matters, how to accept or undo a change. |

### 7.1 Comparison modes

| Mode | Fails when | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact | A listed property differs | Federation settings, a CA policy's conditions and controls, PIM rules |
| Set | Members are added or removed (each change is reported) | Role members, exclusion groups, federated domains, partner tenants, app credentials |
| Count | The count moves outside a tolerance (default: falls by more than 10%) | Groups a policy is *assigned* to, where joiners and leavers are normal |
| Exists | The object is deleted, or changes type (assigned to dynamic) | Every pin, implicitly |

A kind combines them. A CA *inclusion* group is Exists + Exact (`groupTypes`, `membershipRule`) + Count. A CA
*exclusion* group is Exists + Exact + Set on members, because every new member is a bypass. A Set on more than
1,000 members records the count and a hash of the sorted IDs instead of the list; the row then says that the
membership changed but cannot say how, and recommends making the group smaller.

### 7.2 Normalising and volatile properties

Each kind lists the properties it records, never "everything", so a new Graph property never breaks a pin.
Lists are sorted by ID. Timestamps such as `modifiedDateTime` are never recorded. Certificates are stored as
thumbprint plus `NotAfter`. Script content is stored as a SHA-256 hash.

The scan also captures every anchor twice, a few seconds apart, and drops any property whose two readings
differ. Values that change on their own (counters, replication lag) are found on the tenant itself instead of
in a hand-kept ignore list, and the first run after a scan passes.

### 7.3 Direction: weaker or stronger

A drift tool that fails on every change gets switched off. Each kind classifies each change:

| Direction | Result | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weakens | `Failed` | Member added to an exclusion group; CA policy from `enabled` to `enabledForReportingButNotEnforced`; new federated domain; new credential on a privileged app; IP range added to a trusted location; AV exclusion added |
| Expected | `Passed` with a note | The signing certificate is now the pinned `nextSigningCertificate` (a planned rollover); a pinned credential expired and was removed |
| Strengthens or neutral | `Investigate` | Member removed from an exclusion group; new CA policy; MFA requirement added; partner tenant removed |
| Unknown | `Failed` | Anything the kind has no rule for |

`Investigate` keeps the change visible without counting it as a failure. Accepting clears it either way.

### 7.4 Where the code goes

Following the repository layout:

- **Readers** that other checks can reuse, such as `Get-MtDomainFederationConfiguration`, go in
  `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. They call `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` and read through the session
  cache, like every check.
- **Discover, Capture and Compare** for each kind go in `powershell/internal/checks/maester/<service>/`, since
  only the pin families use them.
- **A registry**, `powershell/assets/MaesterPinKinds.psd1`, lists each kind: `Key`, the three function names,
  the recorded properties, the modes and the direction rules. It is the same shape as the measures registry
  (`MaesterMeasures.psd1`).
- **The families** are ordinary native tests in `tests/maester/<service>/`, one per kind, with a new
  attribute property `PinKind` (section 13.1). Their `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `Product`, `Feature`,
  `Severity` and `Mitre` are declared and reviewed against the rubric like any test.

A sketch of a family:

```powershell
function Test-MtPinnedDomainFederation {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that each pinned federated domain keeps its federation settings.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'MT.13xx',
        Title = 'Federated domains should keep their pinned federation settings.',
        PinKind = 'entra.domain-federation',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'hybrid-identity',
        Area = 'identity',
        ResourceType = 'Domain',
        Severity = 'High',
        Mitre = 'T1484.002',
        Service = 'Graph'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The pin to check, supplied by the engine from the pin file.
        $Instance
    )

    Test-MtPin -Instance $Instance   # capture, compare, write the result detail, return $true/$false/$null
}
```

The taxonomy keys in the sketch are placeholders; each family's values are chosen with the rubric when it is
written.

## 8. Deciding what is critical

The scan builds a dependency graph and pins what it reaches. This is what makes the pins specific to the
tenant and the reasons readable.

**Roots** are of two sorts:

- *Controls*: every enabled or report-only CA policy, the authentication methods policy, PIM settings for
  privileged roles, Intune compliance and endpoint security policies, Defender policies, mail flow protection.
- *Ways in*: federated domains, trusted certificate authorities, partner tenants (cross-tenant access, GDAP),
  privileged role members, service principals with high-impact permissions, emergency access accounts.

**Edges** are the references between objects:

```text
CA policy ──include/exclude──▶ user · group · role · named location · auth strength
CA policy ──requires compliant device──▶ Intune compliance policy ──assigned to──▶ group · filter
Intune security policy ──assigned to / excluded──▶ group ──dynamic rule──▶ (the rule itself)
Licensing group ──assigns──▶ SKU ──enables──▶ Entra ID P2 · Intune · Defender for each member
Privileged role ──held by──▶ user · group (role-assignable) · service principal
Service principal ──controlled by──▶ owners · credentials · federated identity credentials
Federated domain ──trusts──▶ issuer · signing certificate
```

**Severity** is the highest severity among the roots that reach the anchor. A group excluded from the
"require MFA for admins" policy is High; a group that only receives a Wi-Fi profile is not reached at all, so it
is not pinned. The reason string names the path ("Excluded from 'CA001 Require MFA for admins' and 3 other
policies"), so an admin can tell why every pin exists.

**Limits.** The scan pins only what it reaches from a root and only the properties the kind lists. Large
inclusion groups are pinned by count. A tenant with 300 CA policies gets 300 policy pins and the groups they
reference, which is the point; the report groups pin rows so they do not crowd out other checks (section 10).

**Emergency access accounts.** With `EmergencyAccessAccounts` set, those accounts are pinned. Without it, the
scan proposes as candidates the cloud-only users who hold Global Administrator and are excluded from every
enabled CA policy, and suggests setting `EmergencyAccessAccounts`. Candidates are written with
`Enabled: false` until the admin confirms them.

## 9. Catalogue of pin kinds

This is the research behind the first milestones. *Why* names what an attacker or a careless change gains.
Permissions marked † are not in `Get-MtGraphScope` today (decision 9).

### 9.1 Ways in (Entra ID)

| Kind | Discovers | Records | Why | Mode | Graph | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.federated-domains` | The tenant's domains | The set of federated domains, and each verified domain's authentication type | A new federated domain, or a managed domain turned federated, is a known persistence route: the attacker's IdP signs in as the domain's users (T1484.002) | Set | `GET /domains` | High |
| `entra.domain-federation` | Each federated domain | Issuer, sign-in and sign-out URIs, signing and next signing certificate, `federatedIdpMfaBehavior`, protocol, `promptLoginBehavior`, signed-request setting | A replaced signing certificate lets its holder forge tokens (T1606.002); `acceptIfMfaDoneByFederatedIdp` hands MFA to the IdP | Exact; rollover to the pinned next certificate is Expected | `GET /domains/{id}/federationConfiguration` | High |
| `entra.cba-trusted-cas` | Certificate-based authentication configurations | Each trusted CA's thumbprint, issuer, root flag, CRL URLs, and the CBA method's issuer and strength bindings | A rogue trusted CA lets someone sign in as any user with a certificate they issued (T1556) | Set + Exact | `GET /directory/publicKeyInfrastructure/certificateBasedAuthConfigurations` (beta) and the authentication methods policy | High |
| `entra.cross-tenant-partners` | Cross-tenant access default and partner settings | The partner tenants; per partner: inbound MFA and device trust, B2B direct connect, inbound user sync | Trusting another tenant's MFA or devices, or letting it sync users in, gives that tenant part of your access control (T1199) | Set + Exact | `GET /policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default`, `/partners` | High for trust or sync, else Medium |

| `entra.directory-sync` | Hybrid tenants | `onPremisesSyncEnabled`, the sync feature flags (such as blocking soft match and cloud-object takeover through hard match), members of Directory Synchronization Accounts | Turning those flags off lets an on-premises account take over a cloud admin (T1556.007) | Exact + Set | `GET /organization`, `GET /directory/onPremisesSynchronization` | High |

| Kind | Discovers | Records | Why | Mode | Graph | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### 9.4 Mail and DNS (milestone 5)

| Kind | Records | Why | Mode | Source | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exchange.transport-rules` | Rules, state, priority, conditions and actions | Redirect, BCC or forward to outside, or SCL -1, is mail exfiltration or a filter bypass (T1114.003) | Set + Exact; external recipients and filter bypass weaken | `Get-TransportRule` | High |
| `exchange.connectors` | Inbound and outbound connectors: smart hosts, TLS, sender IPs and certificates, enhanced filtering | An inbound connector can make mail look internal or skip filtering; an outbound one can route mail through another host | Set + Exact | `Get-InboundConnector`, `Get-OutboundConnector` | High |
| `exchange.forwarding-and-journal` | Remote domains' auto-forward, outbound spam auto-forward mode, journal rules and recipients | Turning on forwarding or adding a journal recipient copies mail out | Exact + Set | `Get-RemoteDomain`, `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy`, `Get-JournalRule` | High |
| `dns.mail-records` | Per accepted domain: MX hosts, SPF, DMARC, DKIM selectors | A changed MX routes mail elsewhere; a new SPF include lets another sender pass as you | Exact | DNS | High for MX, Medium otherwise |

### 9.5 Kinds only the admin or the agent can target

Some anchors matter because of what the business is, not because of a reference. Their kinds exist, but the
scan does not choose targets for them; the admin (`Add-MtTenantPin`) or the agent skill does.

| Kind | Records | Typical targets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entra.user-auth-methods` | Registered method IDs and types, default method | Executives, finance approvers, admins without PIM |
| `entra.app-credentials` | Owners, credential key IDs, federated identity credentials, permissions | Payroll and HR provisioning apps, SCIM connectors, customer-facing apps |
| `exchange.mailbox-access` | Full Access, Send As and Send on Behalf holders; inbox rules that forward or delete (T1114.002) | Executive and shared finance mailboxes |
| `entra.group-members` | Members and owners | Groups that grant access to a sensitive app or site |

Teams external access, SharePoint and OneDrive sharing, and Purview retention and DLP states are candidates
for later kinds.

## 10. Results and the report

Each pin is a row, `MT.13xx.<Target.Id>`, titled with the object's name ("Federated domain contoso.com should
keep its pinned federation settings"). A changed pin's detail looks like this:

```markdown
The federation settings of **contoso.com** changed since they were pinned on 2026-11-09 by admin@contoso.com.

| Setting | Pinned | Now | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| signingCertificate | 3F2A…91 (expires 2027-04-02) | 77C0…1D (expires 2036-11-08) | Weakens |

**Why this is pinned:** contoso.com is federated with AD FS. A different issuer or signing certificate lets
whoever holds it sign in as any user in the domain.

**If you made this change**, accept it: `Update-MtTenantPin -Id MT.13xx.contoso.com`.
**If you did not**, treat it as an incident: restore the certificate and review sign-ins for contoso.com users.
```

The row also gets an additive `Pin` block in the result JSON (schema 2.3): `Kind`, `TargetId`, `PinnedAt`,
`PinnedBy`, `Source`, `Changes` (property, pinned, current, direction) and, from milestone 3, `ChangedBy`.

Pin rows can number in the hundreds, almost all passing. To keep them from inflating the pass rate, the report
shows them in their own *Pinned configuration* section with its own count ("118 unchanged, 3 changed, 1 to
review"), leaves them out of the headline score, and lists changed pins at the top of the items that need
attention (decision 5).

## 11. Who changed it (milestone 3)

A changed pin is far more useful with a name and a time on it. For each changed pin, and only those, Maester
reads the audit records for the pin's target since `PinnedAt` (capped at the log's retention):

| Source | Query | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entra audit log | `GET /auditLogs/directoryAudits?$filter=targetResources/any(t:t/id eq '{id}')` | 30 days with Entra ID P1, 7 days without |
| Intune audit events | `GET /deviceManagement/auditEvents` filtered by resource ID | 1 year |
| Azure activity log | Activity log for the scope | 90 days |
| Exchange admin audit | Purview audit search (asynchronous) | Later |

The row lists up to five records as facts: activity, time, actor (user or app), and the client the change came
from. With nothing found, it says so and gives the retention, so "no record" is not read as "nobody". The reads
go through the session cache like any check and use `AuditLog.Read.All` and `DeviceManagementApps.Read.All`,
which Maester already requests.

## 12. The agent skill

The admin's AI agent is good at what the dependency graph cannot see: which app runs payroll, who the
executives are, what a naming convention means, whether a group called *Finance-Approvers* deserves a pin. The
skill uses that judgement and nothing else.

Workflow of `maester-tenant-pins` (a `SKILL.md` for Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and other agents):

1. Run `New-MtTenantPin -WhatIf` (or `Update-MtTenantPin -Discover -WhatIf`) and read the candidates and the
   tenant summary. The deterministic scan always comes first.
2. Read more of the tenant, read-only, through Maester's connection or a Graph MCP server: titles, app names,
   group names, sign-in volume of apps, mailbox types.
3. Propose extra pins with the kinds in section 9.5, each with evidence ("*Workday Provisioning* has
   `User.ReadWrite.All` and syncs 4,200 users"). Never more than a reviewable handful at a time.
4. Write the accepted ones with `Add-MtTenantPin -Kind … -Target … -Reason …`, which validates the entry and
   marks it `Source: Agent`. The skill never edits the JSON by hand.
5. When nothing in the catalogue fits, write a custom test instead: `New-MtTest`, then check it with
   `Get-MtTest -Path` and `Invoke-MtTest -Path`, as the writing-tests guide describes.

Guardrails written into the skill: read-only on the tenant; no pin without the admin's yes; no secrets in the
file; every proposal cites what it read.

## 13. Changes to Maester

### 13.1 Engine

- **`PinKind` on `[MaesterTest]`.** A family with `PinKind` gets its instances from the pin file: one per
  enabled pin of that kind, `Id` from `Target.Id`, `Title` from the display name, `Severity` from the pin.
  It needs no `InstanceSource`.
- **No pin file, no rows.** Without a pin file for the tenant, pin families get `NotRun` with reason
  `NoPinFile`, not `Skipped`, so a tenant that does not use pins sees nothing new in its report. (A plain
  family would add one `Skipped NoInstances` row per kind to every run.)
- **Wrong tenant**: `Error` with `InvalidConfiguration` on every pin family (section 6).
- **Result schema 2.3**: the `Pin` block (section 10).
- The C# reader gains the property; the committed DLL is rebuilt.

### 13.2 Commands

All in `powershell/public/run/`, with full help:

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `New-MtTenantPin` | Scans and writes a new pin file. `-Kind` limits the kinds; `-WhatIf` returns the candidates without writing; refuses to overwrite an existing file. |
| `Update-MtTenantPin` | Re-records the pins named by `-Id` (row IDs or `-Kind`), or all changed pins with `-All` after showing them. `-Discover` adds new anchors and proposes retiring pins whose object is gone. Shows the diff and honours `-WhatIf`. |
| `Add-MtTenantPin` | Adds one pin of a kind for a target the admin or agent chose, with a reason. |
| `Get-MtTenantPin` | Lists the pins in the file, filtered by kind or ID. |

Checking pins needs no command of its own: `Invoke-Maester` runs them, and `Invoke-MtTest -Id MT.13xx` runs one
kind.

### 13.3 Repository

- One family per kind in `tests/maester/<service>/`, IDs reserved on
  [maester365/maester#697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) before milestone 1.
- `powershell/assets/MaesterPinKinds.psd1` and `powershell/assets/schemas/maester-pins-1.0.json` (path to match
  the other schemas).
- Unit tests: every registry kind has exactly one family with that `PinKind` and the reverse; each kind's
  Compare against fixture pairs, including each direction rule; normalisation is stable (capture the same
  fixture twice, no change); the pin file schema; wrong tenant; missing file.
- Docs: a *Tenant pins* page under `website/docs/` (what, how to scan, how to accept, CI, security of the file),
  each family's guide, and a link from MT.1060's guide.
- The agent skill's home is decision 10.

## 14. Noise, safety and limits

- **First run is clean.** The scan captures twice and drops volatile values (section 7.2); a run straight after
  the scan must have no changed pins, and the lab soak in milestone 1 checks this.
- **Steady state.** Target: fewer than one unexpected changed pin per week on a stable lab tenant over two
  weeks. Any kind that misses it gets its properties or direction rules fixed before it ships.
- **Read-only.** Pins never write to the tenant, and accepting writes only the local file.
- **Session cache.** All reads go through it; no kind bypasses it.
- **The pin file is trusted input.** Whoever can change it can accept a change. The docs recommend branch
  protection and review, the same as for the config. Signing the file is a later option.
- **Licences and connections.** A kind whose service is not connected, or whose licence or permission is
  missing, is skipped with the usual reason; the scan does not propose pins it cannot check.

## 15. Relationship to existing work

- **MT.1060 (drift folders)** stays for admins who supply their own JSON. Pins are the managed form: Maester
  picks, records and compares. Compare can reuse `Compare-MtJsonObject` for Exact properties.
- **`EmergencyAccessAccounts`** seeds the emergency access pins, and the scan suggests values for it.
- **Generic checks** stay the judge of "good". A pin on a weak setting still passes; the generic check fails.
- **`Compare-MtTestResult`** compares two runs' results. Pins compare the tenant with an approved state, so a
  change shows on the first run after it, even with no earlier result.
- **Microsoft's tenant configuration management APIs** (`/admin/configurationManagement`: monitors,
  baselines, drifts and snapshot jobs, `ConfigurationMonitoring.Read.All`, beta) watch the resources an admin
  configures. Maester could later read the drifts of monitors an admin created, as one more source for the
  report. It would not replace pins, which decide what to watch and explain why.

## 16. Milestones

| | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| M1 | Pin file and schema, `PinKind` and `NotRun NoPinFile`, shared `Test-MtPin`, `New-`, `Update-` and `Get-MtTenantPin`, kinds: federated domains, domain federation, CA policies, CA exclusion groups, CA named locations, privileged role members, emergency access. Unit tests and a lab soak. |
| M2 | The rest of 9.1 to 9.3: CBA, cross-tenant, GDAP, directory sync, PIM settings, privileged apps, consents, auth methods, CA inclusion groups, licensing groups, Intune and Defender kinds. |
| M3 | Who changed it (Entra and Intune audit), the `Pin` block and the report section. |
| M4 | `Add-MtTenantPin`, the kinds in 9.5, the agent skill, the docs page. |
| M5 | Exchange, DNS and Azure kinds; the maester-action pull-request flow (in that repository). |
| Later | Teams, SharePoint and Purview kinds; pin kinds shipped by packs; reading Microsoft's configuration drifts. |

## 17. Decisions for the owner

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Name | **Tenant pins** ("pin", "accept"). "Baseline" already means three things in Maester (CIS and Intune baselines, MT.1060's `baseline.json`). Alternatives: watchlist, approved state. |
| 2 | Pin file and kind families, or generated test files, or AI-written tests | **Pin file and families**, with the AI as a proposal layer (section 4) |
| 3 | One family per kind, or one family per service | **Per kind**: own guide, gates, permissions, rubric review, and selection by ID; about 25 MT IDs |
| 4 | `PinKind` in the engine, or a plain `InstanceSource` | **`PinKind`**, so tenants without pins get no new rows |
| 5 | Pin rows in the headline score | **No**: own report section; changed pins listed under needs attention |
| 6 | A tightening change | **`Investigate`**, not `Failed` |
| 7 | File name and place | **`maester-pins.<tenantId>.json`** beside the config, found like the tenant config, never unnamed |
| 8 | Plain values or hashes in the file | **Plain values**, so a change can show from and to; hashes only for script bodies and memberships above 1,000 |
| 9 | `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` and `DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All` | **Add both to the default read scopes**: read-only, and scripts are among the highest-value pins |
| 10 | Where the user-facing agent skill lives | **A root `skills/` folder** in this repository, so skill installers can add it from GitHub; separate from the contributor skills in `.github/skills/` |
| 11 | Audit attribution in M3 | **Yes**, Entra and Intune first |
| 12 | Microsoft's configuration monitors | **Not now**; revisit as a reader once the API is generally available |
