content.text:
I've written the full design in [docs/proposals/tenant-pins.md](docs/proposals/tenant-pins.md). It's a draft and nothing is built yet. The file isn't tracked by git and sits on your website branch (`feat/website-pricing-video-polish`), so leave it out when you commit the website work.

**The core idea.** Today's checks ask "is this set up well?", and the answer is the same for every tenant. This adds a second question: "is this still the way we set it up?" Maester scans the tenant once, records how the important objects look, and fails a test when one changes. I've called these recorded facts "pins".

**What I recommend:**
- **Store the pins as data, not as generated code.** `New-MtTenantPin` writes a file called `maester-pins.<tenantId>.json`, which always carries the tenant ID in its name. Maester ships one family test for each kind of pin (federated domain, CA exclusion group, Intune script, and so on), and each pin becomes a row such as `MT.13xx.contoso.com`. When a pin kind gets better, every tenant gets the fix without regenerating anything.
- **Decide what's critical by following dependencies, not names.** The scan starts from the controls (Conditional Access, MFA, PIM, Intune compliance, Defender) and from the ways in (federation, trusted certificate authorities, partner tenants, privileged apps). It pins whatever those depend on. For example: a CA policy requires a compliant device, so the compliance policies, their assignment groups and filters get pinned too. Each pin's severity and reason come from that chain, e.g. "excluded from 'CA001 Require MFA for admins' and 3 other policies".
- **Keep noise low, or people will turn it off.**
  - A change that weakens security is `Failed`; one that tightens it is `Investigate`.
  - Planned changes, like a federation certificate rolling over to the pinned next certificate, pass with a note.
  - The scan reads everything twice and drops values that change on their own, so the first run is clean.
  - Exclusion groups track every member; groups a policy only targets are tracked by member count, with a tolerance.
- **Accepting a change is a commit.** `Update-MtTenantPin` records the new value, so in CI the pull request is the approval.
- **Show who changed it** (milestone 3). For changed pins only, Maester reads the Entra and Intune audit logs for that object.
- **Use AI as a layer on top.** An agent skill proposes pins that dependencies can't find, like the payroll app's credentials or the CFO's sign-in methods. It uses the same pin kinds, falls back to `New-MtTest` when none fits, and is never involved at run time.

**The research (section 9)** covers about 30 kinds of pins, each with the Graph endpoint, the ATT&CK technique and a severity. They include:
- federation issuer and certificates
- trusted certificate authorities for certificate sign-in
- cross-tenant trust and partner admin access
- directory sync settings
- privileged role members and PIM rules
- privileged apps' credentials and owners
- CA policies, exclusion groups and trusted locations
- licensing groups
- Intune scripts, assignments and filters, and multi-admin approval
- Defender antivirus exclusions
- mail flow rules, connectors and MX records

I checked the endpoints against the Graph API index, not against a live tenant. Two of them need permissions Maester doesn't request today: `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` and `DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All`.

**Section 17 has 12 decisions for you**, each with a recommendation. The ones that shape the build most:
- the name
- a new `PinKind` property on the test attribute, so tenants without a pin file see no new rows
- keeping pin rows out of the headline score
- whether to add those two permissions to the defaults

Microsoft has its own configuration-drift API in beta (`/admin/configurationManagement`). I recommend not building on it for now: it's in preview, creating its monitors needs write access, and it doesn't know why an object matters.

## The idea in one paragraph Maester's checks ask every tenant the same question: **is this configured well?** This idea adds a second question that only your tenant can answer: **is this still the way we set it up?** Maester scans the tenant once, works out which objects its security depends on (the federation trust, the groups excluded from MFA, the Intune policies that decide "compliant", the apps holding Graph write permissions), records how each one looks today, and from then on fails a test the moment one of them changes. Admins get tests written for their own tenant without having to think up what matters. We're calling the recorded facts **pins**. The full design is in the draft PR linked below. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph today["Today: the same checks for every tenant"] G["Is MFA required for admins?
Is legacy auth blocked?
Is DKIM on?"] end subgraph pins["Tenant pins: tests only your tenant has"] P["Is contoso.com still federated with
sts.contoso.com and certificate 3F2A…91?
Does CA-Exclude-BreakGlass still have
exactly bg-01 and bg-02?"] end G -- "is it good?" --> R1(["Pass / Fail"]) P -- "has it changed?" --> R2(["Unchanged / Changed, with who and when"]) ``` ## Why generic checks can't do this | | What a generic check sees | What actually matters in *your* tenant | | --- | --- | --- | | **Federation** | contoso.com is federated with a valid configuration ✅ | Someone swapped the token-signing certificate, or federated a second domain with their own IdP. They can now sign in as your users ([T1484.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1484/002/), [T1606.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1606/002/)). Every setting is still "valid". | | **Exclusion groups** | Every CA policy excludes a break-glass account ✅ | A third account was added to the exclusion group. The membership of an exclusion group *is* the policy. | | **Indirect dependencies** | A CA policy requires a compliant device ✅ | Someone removed the BitLocker requirement from the compliance policy, or edited the assignment filter. The CA policy got weaker without anyone touching it. | MT.1060 can already compare a `baseline.json` with a `current.json`, but you have to know what to export and keep the files up to date yourself. This idea moves all of that into Maester. ## How Maester decides what's critical The scan follows dependencies instead of guessing from names. It starts from two kinds of roots and pins everything they reach: - **Controls**: Conditional Access, the authentication methods policy, PIM, Intune compliance and endpoint security, Defender. - **Ways in**: federation, trusted certificate authorities, partner tenants, privileged roles and apps. ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef root fill:#1f6feb,color:#fff,stroke:#1f6feb classDef anchor fill:#fff8c5,color:#000,stroke:#d4a72c classDef skip fill:#eee,color:#666,stroke:#bbb,stroke-dasharray: 4 3 CA["CA001 Require MFA for admins"]:::root CA3["CA003 Require compliant device"]:::root FED["Federation trust"]:::root ROLE["Global Administrator"]:::root CA -- "excludes" --> EXG["Group: CA-Exclude-BreakGlass
every member pinned"]:::anchor CA -- "skips MFA from" --> LOC["Named location: HQ-Egress
IP ranges pinned"]:::anchor CA3 -- "relies on" --> CP["Compliance policy: Windows
settings pinned"]:::anchor CP -- "assigned to" --> DG["Group: All-Corp-Devices
dynamic rule + count pinned"]:::anchor CP -- "filtered by" --> FL["Filter: Corporate-owned
rule pinned"]:::anchor FED -- "trusts" --> DOM["contoso.com
issuer + signing certs pinned"]:::anchor ROLE -- "held by" --> SP["App: Provisioning-Sync
owners, secrets, federated creds pinned"]:::anchor ROLE -- "held by" --> ADM["3 admins
membership pinned"]:::anchor WIFI["Group used only for a Wi-Fi profile"]:::skip ``` Each pin gets its **severity** from the most important control that reaches it, and a **reason** naming the path, such as *"Excluded from 'CA001 Require MFA for admins' and 3 other policies. A new member skips all of them."* Things no control depends on (the grey box) aren't pinned. ## The lifecycle ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor Admin participant M as Maester participant T as Tenant (read-only) participant Repo as Your Maester repo Admin->>M: New-MtTenantPin M->>T: Scan from controls and ways in M-->>Admin: 63 pins found, each with a reason Admin->>Repo: Commit maester-pins..json loop Every scheduled run M->>T: Read the pinned objects (session cache) M-->>Repo: Report: all pins unchanged ✅ end Note over T: Someone adds a member to CA-Exclude-BreakGlass M->>T: Next run M-->>Admin: ❌ MT.13xx.4b9e… changed
+ bob@contoso.com, added by alice@ via Entra admin center alt Expected change Admin->>M: Update-MtTenantPin -Id MT.13xx.4b9e… M->>Repo: Pull request with the new pinned value else Unexpected Admin->>T: Undo it and investigate end ``` Accepting a change is just a commit to the pin file, so in a repository the pull request **is** the approval. ## Not every change should be a failure A drift tool that fails on every change gets switched off. Each pin kind knows which direction a change goes: ```mermaid flowchart TD C["A pinned value changed"] --> Q{"Which way?"} Q -- "Weakens security
member added to exclusion group
policy set to report-only
new secret on a privileged app
IP range added to trusted location" --> F["❌ Failed"] Q -- "Planned
cert rolled over to the pinned next cert
expired credential removed" --> P["✅ Passed, with a note"] Q -- "Tightens or neutral
member removed from exclusion
new CA policy added" --> I["🔎 Investigate"] Q -- "No rule for it" --> F ``` On top of that, the scan reads every object twice and drops any value that changes on its own, so the first run straight after a scan comes back clean. ## What a changed pin looks like in the report > **❌ Federated domain contoso.com should keep its pinned federation settings** · High > > | Setting | Pinned 2026-11-09 | Now | | > | --- | --- | --- | --- | > | signingCertificate | `3F2A…91` (expires 2027-04-02) | `77C0…1D` (expires 2036-11-08) | Weakens | > > **Why this is pinned:** contoso.com is federated with AD FS. A different issuer or signing certificate lets whoever holds it sign in as any user in the domain. > > **Changed by:** *Set domain authentication* · 2026-11-12 03:14 UTC · app *Unknown client* > > **If you made this change:** `Update-MtTenantPin -Id MT.13xx.contoso.com` · **If you didn't:** treat it as an incident. ## What gets pinned (first pass) | Area | Pins | | --- | --- | | 🚪 **Ways in** | Federated domains · federation issuer and signing certificates · trusted CAs for certificate sign-in · cross-tenant trust and inbound sync · partner admin access (GDAP) · directory sync takeover protections | | 👑 **Privilege** | Members of privileged roles (active and eligible) · PIM activation rules · apps with high-impact permissions: their owners, secrets and federated credentials · tenant-wide consents · emergency access accounts · Azure root and subscription owners | | 🛡️ **Controls** | CA policies · CA exclusion groups (exact members) · CA target groups (rule and count) · trusted named locations · authentication methods and strengths · licensing groups · Intune compliance policies · security policy assignments and filters · Intune scripts and remediations (they run as SYSTEM) · multi-admin approval · Defender antivirus and ASR exclusions | | ✉️ **Mail** | Transport rules · connectors · auto-forwarding and journal rules · MX, SPF and DMARC records | | 🎯 **Admin- or AI-chosen** | Executives' sign-in methods · payroll and HR apps' credentials · executive mailbox access · groups that guard a sensitive app | The design doc has the full catalogue, with the Graph endpoint, permission, ATT&CK technique and severity for each. ## How it fits together ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph scan["Scan (once, then on update)"] NEW["New-MtTenantPin
Update-MtTenantPin -Discover"] SKILL["Agent skill (optional)
proposes extra pins with evidence"] end FILE[("maester-pins.<tenantId>.json
data you review and commit")] subgraph run["Every run"] KINDS["One family test per pin kind
MT.13xx federation, MT.13xx exclusion group, …"] ENG["Engine: one row per pin
NotRun when there is no pin file"] AUD["Audit log lookup
for changed pins only"] end REP["Report: own 'Pinned configuration' section
changed pins at the top"] NEW --> FILE SKILL -- "Add-MtTenantPin" --> FILE FILE --> ENG --> KINDS --> AUD --> REP ``` **Pins are data, not generated code.** We considered having an AI write a test file per object, and generating test files from templates. Both leave every tenant with hundreds of files that go stale the day Maester improves how a check works. With a pin file and one test per kind, the file is small enough to review in a diff, the logic is versioned and unit tested in Maester, and every fix reaches every tenant. **Where AI fits.** An AI agent is good at what dependencies can't show: which app runs payroll, who the executives are, what a naming convention means. A user-facing skill lets your agent propose those pins (using the same kinds, with evidence for each), or write a proper custom test with `New-MtTest` when nothing fits. The AI proposes and you approve. Nothing at run time depends on a model. ## What this isn't - **Not a replacement for the generic checks.** A pin on a weak setting still passes. Pins say "unchanged", not "good". - **Not real-time.** Pins are checked when Maester runs. A SIEM alert is faster, but pins catch changes made by any route, need no SIEM, and record the approved value. - **Not backup or desired-state config.** Pins never write to the tenant and record only what matters to security. ## Open questions The design lists 12 decisions, each with a recommendation. The ones that shape it most: 1. **Name**: "tenant pins"? ("Baseline" already means three things in Maester.) 2. **Engine**: a new `PinKind` attribute property, so tenants without a pin file see no new rows. 3. **Score**: should pin rows stay out of the headline pass rate and get their own report section? 4. **Permissions**: should `DeviceManagementScripts.Read.All` (Intune scripts) and `DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All` (GDAP) be added to the default read scopes? 5. **The agent skill**: should it ship in this repository so skill installers can add it from GitHub? **What would you pin in your tenant that isn't on the list above?** That's the most useful feedback for the catalogue.
